history.summary: Freehold 360-unit CDL development at Hillview MRT, 30 years old, asking $1,787 psf — bang on the $1,787 URA median but at the top of recent transacted range ($1,585-$1,910 psf). The 5.6%/yr URA rate is solid but thin (37 txns), and the $3M quantum for an aging 1,679 sqft FH 4BR points to a slow exit.
history.rating_rationale: Freehold tenure and a real DT-line station (480m) plus a sizeable 360-unit base are genuine positives, and the 5.6%/yr URA rate beats OCR norms. But the unit asks at the very top of the $1,585-$1,910 psf transacted band, the building is 30 years old (maintenance/dated layouts), and $3M for a 1,679 sqft 4BR in D23 is a heavy, niche quantum. The very low score_1000 (193) reflects the age/quantum drag, not a fatal flaw.
red_flags: 30-year-old building — maintenance and dated layout risk

catalysts: Freehold tenure with no lease decay

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Hillview is a quieter residential pocket; 4BR rents to families on the DT line but the tenant pool is moderate. Yield weak on a $3M FH quantum (~2.5-3%).
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: URA 5.6%/yr is encouraging but thin; freehold and DT-line access support steady growth, though top-of-range entry pricing limits near-term upside.
